questions.stem: Which types of electromagnetic radiation are ionising?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet (particularly UV-B and UV-C), X-rays, and gamma rays are ionising radiation. They have enough energy to remove electrons from atoms, which can damage DNA and living cells. The lower-frequency EM waves (radio, microwave, infrared, visible) are non-ionising.

questions.stem: As you move from radio waves to gamma rays across the EM spectrum, what happens to wavelength and frequency?
questions.explanation: Moving from radio waves to gamma rays, wavelength decreases and frequency increases. This is because all EM waves travel at the same speed (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s), so from v = fλ, as frequency increases, wavelength must decrease.
